searchText: _" I understand that eventually home stakers won't be able to produce blocks because they won't be able to compute the KZG commitments to blobs. "_ When would this happen? When they reach a certain size? from https://notes.ethereum.org/@dankrad/new_sharding > Compute KZG proofs for 32 MB of data in ~1s. This requires a 32-64 core CPU. I think a machine that is capable can be built for <5,000$, proof of concept to be implemented. According to conversations with Dag Arne Osvik, it’s likely possible to do this on a GPU much cheaper <dankrad> They will have the tx with commitments. They need to know the data is available to the builder so they can safely include the tx. Simple solution: Builders publish lists of tx or commitments they have data for Harder solution: Build a transaction mempools that allows data availability sampling for transactions

excerpts.author: roberto.bayardo
excerpts.content:
_" I understand that eventually home stakers won't be able to produce blocks because they won't be able to compute the KZG commitments to blobs. "_

When would this happen? When they reach a certain size?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<dankrad> They will have the tx with commitments. They need to know the data is available to the builder so they can safely include the tx.
Simple solution: Builders publish lists of tx or commitments they have data for
Harder solution: Build a transaction mempools that allows data availability sampling for transactions
